stories.title: 1,400 missing in Nepal and Tibet after devastating flood
stories.summary: Nearly 1,400 people, including almost 800 foreigners, are missing across Nepal and Tibet, authorities said, after a wall of mud and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river, sending catastrophic flash floods ⁠through towns and valleys. The devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 359 people, Nepali police said today. Chinese state media had earlier reported three dead in Chinese-controlled Tibet, taking the total killed to at least 362. Rescuers used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off after the floods swept a rugged mountainous region thronged by trekkers and pilgrims linking Lhasa in Tibet with Nepal's capital of Kathmandu. A lake has formed at the site where the flood in Nepal occurred is rising and is at risk of bursting, the country's disaster authority said, as it appealed to residents and rescuers to stay away from the river banks. The blockage of a river yesterday led to the lake's formation, the authority said.

stories.title: Minister, RSA, gardaí to meet on motorway road safety
stories.summary: Senior officials from the Departments of Transport and Justice, as well as gardaí, the Road Safety Authority and Transport Infrastructure Ireland, are to meet on Friday to discuss motorway road safety. The meeting at Leinster House follows a number of recent incidents on the country's motorway network and will be hosted by the Minister of State with responsibility for Road Safety Seán Canney. In a statement, Mr Canney said he wanted to bring key road safety partners together to discuss what can be done to improve safety on motorways. Mr Canney said it is "a complex issue which has many causes" and that it will "not be easily solved".

stories.title: Nvidia forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates
stories.summary: Nvidia has forecast a 70% jump in revenue next fiscal year, underscoring unabated demand for AI computing, while warning that shortages of memory components would continue to curb how quickly it can expand. The chip company's shares rose nearly 5% in extended trading on Wall Street last night, after having dipped over 1% initially. "AI has reached its inflection point. It's doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue," Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang said. The outlook is likely to reassure investors who have questioned how long the AI spending surge can last after years of explosive growth.

After excelling for Ireland in the number 10 jersey during the Guinness Six Nations, Crowley was then absent for the closing stages of Munster's URC campaign and Ireland's opening games in the Nations Championship. Utmost in Munster's thinking is that the player is giving ample time to recover, with head coach Clayton McMillan saying: "Jack Crowley is a very important player for Munster and Ireland with a big future in the game and ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority.

stories.title: Former England ace Sterling on dangerous driving charge
stories.summary: Former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said. Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen. The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported.

stories.title: Leinster have point to prove after Munster mauling
stories.summary: Leinster have learned their lesson ahead of their rematch with Munster in the Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship final on Saturday, according to head coach Sana Govender. Munster thrashed Leinster 39-19 when the sides met in the opening round robin game in Cork three weeks ago, although Munster head coach Matt Brown believes his side caught Leinster "cold" in the seven-try hammering. The province rebounded with a 36-21 win against Connacht before a 75-5 stroll against Ulster to book their place in the decider, and get a shot at revenge against the defending champions, who also beat them in the final in 2025. And their head coach believes they have learned a lot since their defeat in Cork earlier this month.

stories.title: Slí na Samhlaíochta - celebrating the legacy of Manchán Magan
stories.summary: Musical Director Simon O'Reilly introduces Slí na Samhlaíochta/The Way of Imagination, a live performance coming to the National Concert Hall this October that brings together spoken word, music, and visual art in an exploration of the concept of Tír na nÓg through the work of the late author, traveller, broadcaster and documentary maker Manchán Magan. Slí na Samhlaíochta began at the Hedge School Festival in Doolin in 2023, an event I co-founded to bring musicians, writers and visual artists together to create new work. For the closing performance, Manchán Magan brought a spoken-word piece inspired by Tír na nÓg and An Saol Eile, the Otherworld of Irish tradition. Myles O'Reilly and I created a live score around his words, while Crosby Dunkley developed the visuals that accompanied the performance. None of us expected the response. From the opening moments there was a stillness in the room that is difficult to describe. The audience seemed completely immersed and, afterwards, many spoke about how deeply they had been affected. I came away feeling we had created something that deserved another life.

stories.title: Duff did not have 'as much fun' making Bad Sisters

Duff played Grace Williams, the second-eldest sister who is married to the emotionally abusive and coercive John Paul Williams, played by Claes Bang, opposite Sharon Horgan, Eve Hewson, Eva Birthistle and Sarah Greene. The role landed Duff the best supporting actress award at the TV baftas in 2023.

stories.title: Vhi to increase prices by average of 2.75% from October
stories.summary: Vhi is to increase the prices of its health insurance policies by an average of 2.75% from the beginning of October. This will be the provider's second price rise this year, after it announced a 3% average hike across its plans that took effect in March. Vhi is the largest health insurance company in Ireland, with around 1.2 million customers - roughly half of the entire market. The latest increases will see the price of its EnhancedCare 250 plan, which is especially popular among young adults, go up by €22 a year to €1,300 for an adult.

stories.title: Irish woman and her husband found dead at Spanish resort
stories.summary: Police in Spain are investigating the deaths of an Irish woman and her husband at a coastal resort south of Valencia. Homicide squad officers are leading the investigation, although police say the possibility they suffered an accident while they were in a jacuzzi has not yet been ruled out. Their bodies of the woman, aged 45, and the man, aged 50, were discovered yesterday afternoon in a residential estate called Cap Blanc in Cullera, a town of around 25,000 people south of Valencia. Local police were mobilised along with the Civil Guard, the force which is leading the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: Fiscal watchdog 'right' to highlight Govt overspend
stories.summary: The Tánaiste and Minister for Finance has said the Irish Fiscal Advisory Council is "right" to highlight Government budget overspend, but added that "not all spending is the same". The fiscal watchdog warned that the actual budget package is likely to be much larger than what is announced in Budget 2027 on 6 October. Simon Harris also said "we don't ignore their advice, but they're not the Government". He said Ireland lags "somewhere around 25%-30% behind the EU average when it comes to public infrastructure, and our people know that, people who invest in our country know that. So, not all spending is the same".

stories.title: Irish Distillers' annual global net sales dip by 4%
stories.summary: Irish Distillers, which makes Jameson Irish Whiskey, has today reported a global net sales decline of 4% across its portfolio, in line with its parent Pernod Ricard's group performance, for its 2026 financial year to end of June. However, Irish Distillers noted that improved results were evident in the second half of the year. Its other brands include Powers, Middleton, Green Spot and Redbreast whiskeys. Jameson saw net sales growth of 9% across markets outside the US, which the company said demonstrated the brand's continued ability to drive growth in mature and emerging markets, while the US spirits market continued to face soft market conditions.

stories.title: How a glacier collapse may have caused Nepal-Tibet floods
stories.summary: A huge piece of ice that fell thousands of metres from a glacier into a river below may have unleashed the flooding disaster in Nepal and Tibet. A glacier collapse in Nepal's mountains near Tibet appears to have triggered the disaster. "A large chunk of glacier fell from about 5,200 metres... into a valley," said Simon Cox, principal scientist at New Zealand's GNS Science. It "transformed into this raging mass of debris... where it picks up rocks and sediment and trees and anything in the way and fires it on down through the canyon," he said.

stories.title: Rovers must find their form with Europe in the balance
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers are going in search of their first European away win of the season as they look to once again qualify for the group stages of the Conference League. The Hoops carry a 1-1 scoreline into their Conference League play-off second-leg clash against KuPS of Finland after conceding a disappointing late equaliser in Tallaght. That result means, for the first time this season, Rovers didn't win their home leg of a European clash and leaves them with a tricky task of securing victory on the road, something that they have yet to achieve this campaign. Across Champions League and Europa League qualifiers Rovers suffered three away defeats, conceding nine goals and scoring just once in their defeats against Maltese side Floriana (2-0), Ararat Armenia (2-0) and Albania's Egnatia (5-1).

stories.title: Net wealth of households hits record high - Central Bank
stories.summary: Irish household wealth has hit record levels again, but that growth may be coming to an end and inequality remains very high, according to a new Central Bank report. The Central Bank's Irish Household Wealth report for the first quarter of 2026 found that the net wealth of Irish households hit a new record of €1,429.5 billion, up 4% in the first three months of the year. Much of the wealth increase is related to the steady house price growth of recent years. Despite easing rates of increase, property prices continue to rise with the latest figures showing they are 26.5% above the highest level at the peak of the property boom in April 2007. Housing wealth accounts for 66.1% of total net wealth and 59.5% of the total assets of Irish households. It increased by €14.1 billion over the quarter, largely due to positive revaluations.

stories.title: Transfers: Liverpool and PSG agree deal for Barcola
stories.summary: Liverpool have reached an outline agreement with Paris St Germain for Bradley Barcola worth up to £120million. The Reds have been pursuing a deal for the 23-year-old France winger this summer and made a breakthrough in talks on Wednesday evening. A guaranteed fee just over £100m has been agreed in principle along with add-ons that could take the package up to £120m, but there remains work to do to complete the deal as details are ironed out. PSG had initially wanted in the region of £145m for Barcola, who spent the summer at the World Cup with France and scored three goals.

stories.title: McManus: Some county boards view hurling as a 'nuisance'
stories.summary: Former Antrim hurler Neil McManus believes that some county boards regard hurling as a "nuisance" and that counties that ignore the game should be penalised in terms of grants from Croke Park. At the elite level, the 2026 hurling championship was widely viewed as an unsatisfying affair, with an unusually high number of lop-sided games in the Munster championship, culminating in a drab All-Ireland final. While there had been humdrum hurling championships in the past, in 2026 an unflattering light was cast by a newly invigorated football championship, where both the playing rules and the competition format had contributed to one of the most exciting seasons in living memory. Some observers have contended that the commentariat are over-reacting to a single underwhelming campaign but McManus feels the sport has deeper structural issues that need addressing.
